title: Can Teachers Really Detect ChatGPT? The Truth About AI Detectors 🤖 #shorts
description:
AI detectors don't know who wrote your essay. They estimate how predictable your words are (perplexity) and how much your sentence lengths vary (burstiness), then guess. That's why they make mistakes: clear, simple writing can look like AI, and a Stanford study found detectors flagged essays by non-native English writers far more often. OpenAI even shut down its own AI text classifier in 2023 because of its low accuracy. A detector score is a guess, not proof, so keep your drafts and version history.

lines: Your essay goes through an AI detector. It says ninety two percent AI. But you wrote every single word.
Detectors don't actually know who wrote it. They measure how predictable your words are.
AI picks the most likely next word, so its writing is smooth and predictable. If your sentences are predictable too, the detector gets suspicious.
They also check burstiness. Humans mix long and short sentences. AI tends to keep them even.
That's why they fail. Clear, simple writing can look like AI. One study found non-native English writers were flagged far more often. Even OpenAI shut down its own detector for low accuracy.
A detector score is a guess, not proof.
Save your drafts. They're your best evidence.
